## 分诊 · `domain:services` / `priority:p2` + `security` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed — and the read locates the mechanism the card says was not located.**

`origin/main` `f1d7872`, 2026-09-04T23:45:36Z. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts:8-13`, in its own header:

> These are declared by **better-auth**, a third-party dependency on its own release cadence, and the plugin mounts them with a single catch-all — **`rawApp.all(\`${basePath}/*\`)`** — so there are no per-route registration calls to capture …

⇒ **That catch-all is why `/api/v1/auth/definitely-not-a-route-1989` answers `200 {}` instead of 404.** Every path under the auth base path is claimed by one handler; when better-auth's router does not recognise the tail, nothing 404s, because from the HTTP framework's point of view the route *was* matched. The empty body is the fall-through, not a response.

That is the finding's root, it is in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth` ⇒ `domain:services`, and it means **observation 1 is a framework-side defect, not a cloud-composition artifact.** The card's "Step 1: reproduce on a framework-side boot" is still the right first move — but it is now a confirmation step, not an open question about where this lives.

**Second read, which sharpens observation 2.** The ledger already carries all three of the vacuous routes as expected members of the surface:

```
auth-route-ledger.ts:314  'GET  /api/v1/auth/admin/list-users'
auth-route-ledger.ts:363  'POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-role'
auth-route-ledger.ts:367  'POST /api/v1/auth/admin/update-user'
```

alongside the two that answered a real guarded 403 (`:352 ban-user`, `:364 set-user-password`), and `:212` comments on the `/admin/create-user`, `/admin/ban-user`, `/admin/set-user-password` group specifically. ⇒ The three vacuous routes are **declared present and measured absent**. That is a ledger/reality divergence on the repo's most security-relevant namespace, and the ledger exists precisely because a prefix claim cannot tell you whether a route resolves (its header: *54 SDK methods matched on nothing stronger than "something under /auth is claimed"*).

### Grade — p2 with `security`

- **Not p1, and the card earns that with its own control.** Nothing an ordinary member sent changed any row — read back from the sqlite file with the server stopped, every target row byte-unchanged — and the **platform admin got the same vacuous 200**, which is what proves absence rather than silent permissiveness. ⛔ Nobody should re-file this as a privilege escalation; the disproof is already on the card.
- **Not p3.** A nonexistent path answering 200 is the silent-success shape on the **admin** surface: `res.ok`, `status === 200`, "no error thrown" all read a typo'd or renamed admin endpoint as a completed admin action. And better-auth is a third-party dependency **on its own release cadence** — the ledger's header cites this repo already chasing better-auth 1.7 drift in #3624 / #3647. A renamed upstream admin route would therefore go from "works" to "silently does nothing" with no wire signal at all. That is the case this card is really about.
- **`security` label** because it distorts security *measurement*, which the card states exactly: a vacuous 200 makes a future probe conclude "admitted" and file a false p0, or conclude "refused" and miss a real one — and the control that tells them apart is one no ordinary caller can run.

### Boundary test — two halves, and only one is free

- **Observation 1 (nonexistent path ⇒ 404)** narrows the accept set and restores declared = enforced. Bug, ordinary lane work. ⚠️ But it is a **published wire-behaviour change**: something today receiving `200 {}` would start receiving 404, and the catch-all is deliberate architecture (there is no route table to enumerate — the header says the live `auth.api` instance *is* the route table). So the shape is "ask better-auth's instance whether it owns this path, 404 when it does not", not "add a 404 arm". ⛔ Do not narrow the catch-all itself; that is how the surface loses routes on the next better-auth minor.
- **Observation 2 (three declared routes resolving to nothing)** is a different question and may not be a code change at all — it may be that this composition legitimately does not mount them, in which case the ledger is what is wrong. ⇒ Measure before repairing, and be prepared for the answer to be "fix the ledger".

⚠️ These two travel together on one card because the same boot reproduces both and observation 1 is what makes observation 2 unmeasurable — but if observation 2 turns out to be a composition question rather than a framework one, **split it out rather than blocking the 404 fix on it.** Recorded now so the taker does not have to re-derive the split criterion.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only. ⛔ Not adjudicated: this seat does not rule on security-boundary questions.

## Claim

Taking this. Session `01XpTx2tbq3pZRYAdoGt6E6Y`, branch **`claude/issue-15417-auth-catchall-404`** (pushed empty first as the write-route probe; all work lands there).

Re-read the existing comments before claiming — one triage comment from the routing seat, no other claim. The shared identity means the assignee field is not proof, so the branch name above is the identity bit.

Plan, following the triage's recorded split criterion:

1. **Confirm, do not re-derive** the catch-all mechanism (`rawApp.all(\`${basePath}/*\`)`) on a **framework-side** boot — the card's Step 1 — with a nonexistent path as the control.
2. **Half 1 (the one to land):** ask better-auth's live `auth.api` instance whether it owns the path and 404 when it does not. ⛔ The catch-all mount itself stays exactly as wide as it is.
3. **Half 2:** measure whether `admin/list-users` · `admin/set-role` · `admin/update-user` are absent framework-side too. If it is a composition question rather than a framework one, it gets split into its own card and half 1 lands without it.

Published wire-behaviour change ⇒ the changeset says so in the upgrade-note register.

## ⚠️ Premise correction — this card's headline row does NOT reproduce on a framework-side boot

The card's own "Step 1" was run first, and it went the other way. Recording it here before the PR lands, because anyone re-reading this card from the top would otherwise carry away a measurement that is wrong for the framework.

On a framework-side boot (`@objectstack/verify` + showcase, as member and as platform-admin):

```
POST /api/v1/auth/admin/definitely-not-a-route-1989   ->  404, zero-length body, no content-type
```

**404, not `200 {}`.** The boot is comparable and the card's other rows reproduce exactly — `ban-user` and `set-user-password` still give the member `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, and the positive control `POST /auth/update-user` still gives `200 {"status":true}` with the write read back from the store. So the vacuous 200 is specifically absent, not masked by an incomparable stack.

⇒ **The vacuous 200 is a property of a composition, not of the framework mount.** ⛔ Triage's reading that "observation 1 is a framework-side defect, not a cloud-composition artifact" is the part that does not survive measurement — stated here rather than left for someone to re-derive.

### But the investigation found a real defect, and a sharper one

The mechanism is not the catch-all's **width** — it is its **yield**. Since #4088 the catch-all is deliberately non-terminal and hands the request on whenever better-auth answers 404, **with only the status to go on**. Add one broad downstream mount (`app.all('/api/v1/*')` → `200 {}`, the shape a composition adds) and the card's row reproduces on the real stack.

⭐ **And so does something the card never named.** `POST /auth/delete-user` — a route better-auth genuinely **SERVES**, whose 404 means *"`user.deleteUser` is unconfigured"* (`auth-route-ledger`'s `disabled` disposition) — **also came back `200 {}`**. Every 404 a *routed* endpoint produced was replaceable by another route's answer. That is a framework defect, it is independent of which composition you run, and it is what PR [#15918](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15918) fixes: the catch-all now asks better-auth's live `auth.api` whether it owns the path and yields **only when it does not**.

⛔ The mount is untouched and still claims exactly `${basePath}/*` — triage's instruction not to narrow the catch-all is honoured. #4088's surface (`/auth/me/permissions`, `/auth/me/localization`) is unaffected and pinned.

### Half 2: the ledger is right, and no row was deleted

Triage said to measure before repairing and to be prepared for the answer to be *"fix the ledger"*. Measured, the answer is the opposite: the three declared-but-absent routes are **configuration-dependent** — absent with the admin plugin off, present and answering real vendor 403s with it on. `BETTER_AUTH_MOUNTED_SURFACE` is pinned at the maximal config and its own header already says a smaller deployment serving a subset is correct. ⇒ Split to **#15920** (a sub-issue of this card) as the wire-silence problem it actually is: the family is absent on any composition without the admin plugin and **nothing on the wire says so** — a 404 with a zero-length body, byte-identical to a path that never existed, while the SDK can still build those URLs. `auth-route-ledger.ts` diff count is **0**.

### One correction the end-to-end run caught that no review would have

The dev's first draft claimed the nine `/admin/oauth2/*` endpoints were protected examples. Measured, **all nine carry `SERVER_ONLY: true`**, so better-call never routes them and their 404 correctly **stays yieldable**. Prose corrected and a dedicated pin added. ⭐ Worth noting the shape: a claim about which routes exist was wrong in a way only booting the thing could reveal.

### Still open after the fix — a maintainer's call, ⛔ not a lane's

A path better-auth does **not** own is still yielded, so on a composition with a broad downstream mount a genuinely nonexistent auth path still answers that mount's `200 {}` — the exact row this card opened on. Three options, and two of them touch recorded decisions:

- **A — leave it.** The composition owns what it mounts, and #4088's ordering-independence stays exactly as written. The framework already answers 404 on its own.
- **B — yield only to a NON-wildcard downstream registration.** Closes this card's control row, but changes #4088's contract from *"yield to whatever matched"* to *"yield to whatever specifically claimed this path"*, and could break a composition that deliberately mounts e.g. `/api/v1/auth/oidc/*` as a wildcard. ⚠️ #4088 was established for a live product surface — objectui's whole permission layer reads `/auth/me/permissions`.
- **C — give the auth namespace's 404 the ADR-0112 envelope.** ⚠️ This is an explicit **reversal**: `vendor-admin-refusal-envelope.ts` already considered enveloping 404 on this exact namespace and deliberately excluded it (*"a 404 discloses nothing that needs a code"*). This card supplies evidence that reasoning did not have — **an empty body with no content-type is precisely what a downstream layer rewrites into `200 {}`** — but re-opening a recorded narrowing is not a lane decision.

⇒ Recorded on this seat's awaiting-maintainer list. The card is not closed by PR #15918.

## Landed — `d4c2cb196` — and this card stays OPEN, because what landed is not what the card reported

PR [#15918](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/15918) is on `main`: `fix(plugin-auth): the auth catch-all yields only a 404 that disclaims ownership (#15918)`. Landing authority `git log origin/main | grep -c '(#15918)'` = 1, cwd control `(#15365)` = 1. `pm:dispatched` → **`pm:on-hold`**; `bug`, `priority:p2`, `security`, `domain:services` unchanged, read back to confirm.

### ⚠️ Read this before citing the card

⛔ **The card's headline row does not reproduce on a framework-side boot.** `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/definitely-not-a-route-1989` answers **404, zero-length body, no content-type** — not the reported `200 {}`. The boot was comparable and every other row of the card reproduced (`ban-user` and `set-user-password` 403 for the member; the positive control `POST /auth/update-user` 200 with the write read back from the store), so the vacuous 200 is **specifically absent**, not masked. ⇒ The vacuous 200 is a property of a **composition**, and triage's reading that *"observation 1 is a framework-side defect, not a cloud-composition artifact"* is the part that did not survive measurement.

### What actually shipped — a sharper defect the card never named

The mechanism is not the catch-all's **width**, it is its **yield**. Since #4088 the catch-all is deliberately non-terminal and hands the request on whenever better-auth answers 404, **with only the status to go on**. So a 404 that a **routed** endpoint produced — carrying real meaning, e.g. `POST /auth/delete-user`'s *"`user.deleteUser` is unconfigured"* — was replaceable by whatever a downstream mount answered. Measured: with `app.all('/api/v1/*') → 200 {}` installed, `delete-user` came back **`200 {}`**.

The catch-all now asks better-auth's live `auth.api` whether it owns the path and yields **only when it does not**. ⛔ The mount is untouched and still claims exactly `${basePath}/*` — triage's instruction not to narrow it is honoured, and #4088's ordering-independence is intact and pinned.

The review measured the ownership table against better-call's own router over **9282 (method, path) pairs** with **0 divergences in the yield direction**, and one bounded divergence the other way — trailing-slash and doubled-slash spellings of paths better-auth **does** own are now claimed rather than yielded, which the changeset carves out explicitly.

### Why `pm:on-hold` rather than closed or back in the queue

Two things remain and both are **maintainer** calls, so leaving this at `pm:queue` would invite a lane seat to decide one:

1. **The wildcard-yield question.** A path better-auth does *not* own is still yielded, so on a composition with a broad downstream mount a genuinely nonexistent auth path still answers that mount's `200 {}` — the exact row this card opened on. Option **B** (yield only to a non-wildcard registration) changes #4088's contract from *"yield to whatever matched"* to *"yield to whatever specifically claimed this path"*, and #4088 backs a live product surface — objectui's whole permission layer reads `/auth/me/permissions`. ⚠️ Option **C** (envelope the 404) is an explicit **reversal**: `vendor-admin-refusal-envelope.ts` already considered enveloping 404 on this namespace and deliberately excluded it, *"a 404 discloses nothing that needs a code"*. ⭐ This card supplies evidence that reasoning did not have — **an empty body with no content-type is precisely what a downstream layer rewrites into `200 {}`** — but re-opening a recorded narrowing is not a lane decision.
2. **#15928** — the `@objectstack/hono` adapter's `/auth/*` mount carries the **identical unconditioned yield** and is untouched. The defect travels with the yield, not with the mount.

### Half 2 went the opposite way from what triage expected

Triage said to measure before repairing and to be ready for the answer to be *"fix the ledger"*. Measured, the ledger is **right**: the three declared-but-absent routes are **configuration-dependent** — absent with the admin plugin off, present and answering real vendor 403s with it on. **No ledger row was deleted** (`auth-route-ledger` diff count 0). Split to **#15920**, where the review also recorded that `BETTER_AUTH_MOUNTED_SURFACE` counts nine `SERVER_ONLY` rows as "published" though better-call never routes them — which bears on that card's premise.

⭐ **One correction only an end-to-end run could produce:** the first draft claimed the nine `/admin/oauth2/*` endpoints were protected examples. Measured, **all nine carry `SERVER_ONLY: true`**, so better-call never routes them and their 404 correctly **stays yieldable**. A claim about which routes exist, wrong in a way no amount of reading would have caught.
